title: ASP.NET Core
sub: No context, but still no blocking
cards/0/body:
ASP.NET Core has no SynchronizationContext: any free pool thread runs the continuation after await. So the classic .Result deadlock doesn't happen here.

Old ASP.NET (Framework) did have a context, and .Result hung there just like in WPF.
cards/1/task: A request handler calls .Result. Run it to the end: will it hang?
cards/2/options/0: The continuation doesn't need a particular thread: any pool thread will run it
cards/2/options/2: .Result works like await in ASP.NET Core
cards/2/explain: No context, so nothing is waiting on a main thread.
cards/3/body: While a request is stuck on .Result, its pool thread is busy doing nothing. A hundred such requests and the pool starves: new requests wait in the queue even though the CPU is free. It's the same pool starvation from unit 4.
cards/4/task: Rewrite the handler to use await and run it to the end.
cards/5/q: The server crawls under load, but the CPU is at 5%. The code has lots of .Result. What's going on?
cards/5/options/0: Pool threads are blocked, and new requests can't get a thread
cards/5/explain: Classic pool starvation. The cure is await all along the chain.
cards/6/title: HttpContext lives only during the request
cards/6/body: Don't carry HttpContext or scoped services (like DbContext) into a background task: the request ends and they get disposed. Copy the data you need up front, and hand background work to a BackgroundService or a queue.
cards/7/explain: The DbContext is disposed when the request ends, but the background task will still be using it.
cards/8/q: Which are true about ASP.NET Core? Select all that apply.
cards/8/options/1: .Result doesn't cause the classic deadlock, but it blocks a pool thread
cards/8/options/2: ConfigureAwait(false) in app code changes nothing
cards/8/options/3: HttpContext is safe to use after the response
cards/8/explain: You must not use HttpContext after the request ends.
